expected.description: American photographer, writer and LGBT activist
expected.bio: Katherine Lahusen was an American photographer, writer and gay rights activist. She was the first openly lesbian American photojournalist. Under Lahusen's art direction, photographs of lesbians appeared on the cover of The Ladder for the first time. It was one of many projects she undertook with partner Barbara Gittings, who was then The Ladder's editor. As an activist, Lahusen was involved with the founding of the Gay Activists Alliance (GAA) in 1970 and the removal of homosexuality from the American Psychiatric Association's Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM). She contributed writing and photographs to a New York–based Gay Newsweekly and Come Out!, and co-authored two books: The Gay Crusaders in 1972 with Randy Wicker and Love and Resistance: Out of the Closet into the Stonewall Era, collecting their photographs with Diana Davies in 2019.

changes.description: Photographer and gay-rights activist who documented the early equality movement, worked on The Ladder and helped establish the Gay Activists Alliance.
changes.bio: Kay Tobin Lahusen was a photographer, writer and organizer. She photographed and reported for The Ladder and Gay Newsweekly and co-authored The Gay Crusaders. Her papers and photographs are preserved with Barbara Gittings's archive at the New York Public Library.
changes.lgbti_details: NYPL documents Lahusen's photographs of early gay-rights demonstrations and her work for The Ladder. It also records her co-founding of the Gay Activists Alliance in 1970, linking her photography and organizing directly to LGBTQ history.

de.lgbti_details: Die NYPL dokumentiert Lahusens Fotos früher Demonstrationen für die Rechte homosexueller Menschen und ihre Arbeit für The Ladder. Sie hält auch ihre Mitgründung der Gay Activists Alliance 1970 fest und verbindet damit Fotografie und Organisation mit LGBTQ-Geschichte.

expected.bio: Eileen Myles is an American poet and writer who has produced more than twenty volumes of poetry, fiction, non-fiction, libretti, plays, and performance pieces over the last three decades. Novelist Dennis Cooper has described Myles as "one of the savviest and most restless intellects in contemporary literature." The Boston Globe described them as "that rare creature, a rock star of poetry." They won the Lambda Literary Award for Lesbian Fiction in 2011 for their Inferno  In 2012, Myles received a Guggenheim Fellowship to complete Afterglow, which gives both a real and fantastic account of a dog's life. Myles has been called "a cult figure to a generation of post-punk female writer-performers" and uses they/them pronouns.

changes.description: Poet and novelist whose contribution to LGBTQ literature was recognised in Lambda Literary's 2016 Pioneer Award announcement, alongside four earlier Lambda awards.
changes.bio: Eileen Myles writes poetry and fiction, including Chelsea Girls and I Must Be Living Twice. Lambda Literary named Myles its 2016 Pioneer Award honoree and listed a Guggenheim Fellowship among their distinctions.
changes.lgbti_details: Lambda Literary's 2016 Pioneer Award announcement identifies Myles's impact on LGBT culture and a new generation of writers. It also records four previous Lambda Literary Awards, documenting a connection through literary work and its reception.

expected.bio: Olivia Laing is a British writer, novelist and cultural critic. They are the author of five works of non-fiction, To the River, The Trip to Echo Spring, The Lonely City, Everybody, The Garden Against Time, as well as an essay collection, Funny Weather, and a novel, Crudo. In 2018, they were awarded the Windham-Campbell Literature Prize for non-fiction and in 2019, the 100th James Tait Black Memorial Prize for Crudo. In 2019 they became an elected Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

changes.description: Writer whose book Everybody: A Book about Freedom examines gay rights and sexual liberation as part of a wider history of bodies, resistance and freedom.
changes.bio: Olivia Laing is the author of Everybody: A Book about Freedom. The book follows Wilhelm Reich's life to explore bodily freedom, feminism and civil rights, bringing figures including Christopher Isherwood and Susan Sontag into the discussion.
changes.lgbti_details: The description of Everybody published by City Lights explicitly includes gay rights and sexual liberation among the book's subjects. This documents Laing's connection through writing about LGBTQ history within a wider account of bodily freedom.

expected.bio: Ariana DeBose is an American actress and singer. She has received various accolades, including an Academy Award, a British Academy Film Award, and a Golden Globe Award, in addition to nominations for a Tony Award and two Primetime Emmy Awards. In 2022, Time magazine named her one of the 100 most influential people in the world.

expected.bio: Shane Gilberto Jenek, better known under the stage name Courtney Act, is an Australian drag queen, singer and television personality. Courtney first came to prominence competing on the first season of Australian Idol in 2003. After the show, she signed to BMG Australia, and she released her debut single, "Rub Me Wrong", which peaked at No. 29 on the ARIA Singles Chart and was certified Gold. While auditioning for Australian Idol, she became the first "openly queer and gender diverse contest" to openly appear on the show. In 2014, Courtney was one of the runners-up in season six of RuPaul's Drag Race. Courtney is a member of the drag girl-group, The AAA Girls.

changes.lgbti_details: In a GQ interview, Act discusses hosting The Bi Life and challenging stereotypes about bisexual people. The programme and interview connect Act’s work to bisexual visibility and the representation of LGBTQ lives on television.

expected.bio: Pedro Almodóvar Caballero is a Spanish film director, screenwriter and author. His films are distinguished by melodrama, irreverent humour, bold colour, glossy décor, quotations from popular culture, and complex narratives. Desire, LGBTQ issues, passion, family, motherhood, and identity are among Almodóvar's most frequently explored subjects. As one of the most internationally successful Spanish filmmakers, Almodóvar and his films have developed a cult following.

changes.bio: Pedro Almodóvar emerged from Spain's post-Franco cultural movement, La Movida Madrileña. His films include Law of Desire, All about My Mother and Talk to Her, combining distinctive visual style with stories about relationships, gender and sexuality.
changes.lgbti_details: The BFI describes Almodóvar's cinema as a celebration of LGBT lives. Its guide highlights the gay and trans central characters in Law of Desire and the trans representation in All about My Mother, documenting a connection through film.

expected.bio: Lyra Catherine McKee was a journalist from Northern Ireland who wrote for several publications about the consequences of the Troubles. She also served as an editor for Mediagazer, a news aggregator website. On 18 April 2019, McKee was fatally shot while observing rioting in the Creggan area of Derry.

expected.bio: Adrienne Cecile Rich was an American poet, essayist and feminist. She was called "one of the most widely read and influential poets of the second half of the 20th century", and was credited with bringing "the oppression of women and lesbians to the forefront of poetic discourse". Rich criticized the rigid identities that are sometimes created by feminism, called for feminism that is flexible and open to being transformed, and drew attention to the existing current of solidarity and creativity among women, which she named the "lesbian continuum".

changes.description: Poet and essayist whose role in lesbian literary culture includes editing Sinister Wisdom with Michelle Cliff, documented in Lambda Literary Review.

changes.lgbti_details: Susan Stinson's remembrance in Lambda Literary Review records Rich's work with Michelle Cliff as editors and publishers of the lesbian feminist journal Sinister Wisdom. This supplies a concrete connection through lesbian publishing and literary culture.

expected.bio: Alice Nkom is a Cameroonian lawyer, politician, and human rights activist known for her advocacy in defending the rights of LGBTQ+ individuals in Cameroon. She is the first woman in Central Africa to become a lawyer and is noted for her efforts in advocating for the decriminalization of homosexuality in the region.

changes.lgbti_details: Amnesty identifies Nkom as the founder of ADEFHO, an association defending LGBTI people in Cameroon. Its report documents the threats facing her work and the people assisting her, establishing a connection through sustained rights advocacy.

de.bio: Alice Nkom ist eine kamerunische Anwältin und Menschenrechtsverteidigerin. Amnesty dokumentiert die Gründung von ADEFHO 2003 und ihre Auszeichnung mit dem Menschenrechtspreis von Amnesty Deutschland 2014 für den Einsatz für LGBTI-Menschen.

expected.bio: Lili Ilse Elvenes, better known as Lili Elbe, was a Danish painter, transgender woman, and one of the earliest recipients of gender-affirming surgery.

changes.lgbti_details: Loyola University's account of the Lili Elbe Digital Archive places Elbe's life story within transgender history. It explains how editions in Danish, German and English shaped that narrative, documenting her connection through a preserved personal history.

de.lgbti_details: Die Loyola University ordnet Elbes Lebensgeschichte im Lili Elbe Digital Archive in die trans Geschichte ein. Sie erläutert, wie dänische, deutsche und englische Ausgaben die Erzählung formten, und belegt so die Verbindung durch eine bewahrte persönliche Geschichte.
de.bio: Lili Elbe war eine dänische Künstlerin, deren Lebensgeschichte 1931 in Kopenhagen als Fra Mand til Kvinde erschien. Das Lili Elbe Digital Archive vergleicht dänische, deutsche, britische und amerikanische Ausgaben sowie deren redaktionelle und sprachliche Entscheidungen.

expected.bio: Madeline Davis was an American LGBT activist and historian. In 1970 she was a founding member of the Mattachine Society of the Niagara Frontier, the first gay rights organization in Western New York. Davis became the first openly lesbian delegate at a major party national convention, speaking at the 1972 Democratic National Convention. The same year, she taught with Margaret Small the first course on lesbianism in the United States, titled "Lesbianism 101" at the University at Buffalo.

changes.description: Gay-rights activist who founded an archive in 2001 to preserve the history of LGBTQ communities in Western New York and Southern Ontario.
changes.bio: Madeline Davis founded the LGBT Archives of Western New York in 2001. Transferred to Buffalo State's E. H. Butler Library in 2009, the collection preserves photographs, organizational records and other materials documenting regional LGBTQ life.
changes.lgbti_details: Buffalo State's library records that Davis founded the LGBT Archives of Western New York in 2001. Its purpose was to collect, safeguard and share LGBTQ community history, providing a concrete connection through activism and preservation.

sources.basis: Buffalo State's library records that Davis founded the LGBT Archives of Western New York in 2001. Its purpose was to collect, safeguard and share LGBTQ community history, providing a concrete connection through activism and preservation.

de.lgbti_details: Die Bibliothek von Buffalo State dokumentiert, dass Davis 2001 das LGBT Archives of Western New York gründete. Es sollte LGBTQ-Geschichte sammeln, schützen und zugänglich machen. Das belegt die Verbindung durch Aktivismus und die Bewahrung von Community-Geschichte.
de.bio: Madeline Davis gründete 2001 das LGBT Archives of Western New York. Die Sammlung ging 2009 an die E. H. Butler Library von Buffalo State und bewahrt Fotos, Organisationsunterlagen und weitere Zeugnisse des regionalen LGBTQ-Lebens.

expected.bio: Klaus Wowereit (born 1 October 1953) is a German politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPD) and was the Governing Mayor of Berlin from 21 October 2001 to 11 December 2014. In 2001 state elections his party won a plurality of the votes, 29.7%. He served as President of the Bundesrat (the fourth highest office in Germany) in 2001/02.

changes.lgbti_details: A June 2001 Guardian report documents Wowereit's public coming-out before fellow Social Democrats during the Berlin mayoral campaign. His own statement, rather than speculation about his private life, establishes the connection.

de.bio: Klaus Wowereit ist ein deutscher SPD-Politiker und ausgebildeter Jurist. Im Berliner Wahlkampf 2001 bezeichnete er sich öffentlich als schwul und löste damit eine Debatte über Offenheit und Sexualität in der deutschen Politik aus.

de.lgbti_details: In einem Interview zum Life Ball erläutert Keszler die Unterstützung von Aids-Hilfsorganisationen und den Einsatz für Vielfalt und Toleranz. Er fordert auch die Akzeptanz gleichgeschlechtlicher Beziehungen. Das belegt die Verbindung durch öffentlichen Einsatz und Spendenarbeit.
de.bio: Gery Keszler gründete den Life Ball und die gemeinnützige Organisation LIFE+. Zum 25-jährigen Jubiläum 2018 beschrieb er die Verbindung aus Aufklärung, Unterhaltung und Unterstützung für HIV/Aids-Hilfsorganisationen.

expected.bio: Joël Gustave Nana Ngongang (1982–2015), frequently known as Joel Nana, was a leading African LGBT human rights advocate and HIV/AIDS activist.

changes.description: Cameroonian human-rights advocate known as Joel Nana, whose leadership of AMSHeR advanced LGBTI rights and access to HIV services in Africa.
changes.bio: Joel Nana was the founding Executive Director of African Men for Sexual Health and Rights and served from 2009 to 2014. A law graduate, he promoted engagement with African human-rights institutions and access to health services for marginalized communities.
changes.lgbti_details: UNAIDS documents Nana's leadership of African Men for Sexual Health and Rights from 2009 to 2014. It credits his work for the health and human rights of gay men and other men who have sex with men, establishing a direct advocacy connection.

de.description: Kamerunischer Menschenrechtsaktivist, bekannt als Joel Nana, der als Leiter von AMSHeR LGBTI-Rechte und den Zugang zu HIV-Versorgung in Afrika förderte.
de.lgbti_details: UNAIDS dokumentiert Nanas Leitung von African Men for Sexual Health and Rights von 2009 bis 2014. Die Organisation würdigt seinen Einsatz für Gesundheit und Menschenrechte schwuler Männer und anderer Männer, die Sex mit Männern haben, und belegt damit seine Arbeit für die Community.
de.bio: Joel Nana war Gründungsdirektor von African Men for Sexual Health and Rights und leitete die Organisation von 2009 bis 2014. Der Jurist förderte die Zusammenarbeit mit afrikanischen Menschenrechtsinstitutionen und den Zugang benachteiligter Gruppen zu Gesundheitsdiensten.
